title: pvUnstructuredCellTypes
body:
## pvUnstructuredCellTypes

Generates an unstructured grid made of one chosen cell type (linear, quadratic, Lagrange or Bezier lines, triangles, quads, tetrahedra, hexahedra, wedges, pyramids, polyhedra…) by filling a BlocksDimensions grid of unit blocks starting at the origin; one block may hold several cells (e.g. six pyramids). Point arrays "DistanceToCenter" and "Polynomial" give known fields. Use it to test how filters, writers or renderers handle a specific cell type or element order.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Lagrange tetrahedral meshes are not always conformal at block boundaries, as the native documentation warns.
- 1-D types use only the first blocks dimension and 2-D types the first two.
- Schemaxis generates this source from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for it, so inspect the output before relying on it.

Native constructor: `UnstructuredCellTypes`. Identity: `sources/UnstructuredCellTypes`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Addnodestocompletepolynomialbasis` | When true, some quadratic Lagrange cell types will have additional nodes. Specifically, triangles will have 7 points instead of 6; tetrahedra will have 15 points instead of 10; and wedges will have 21 points instead of 18. These additional points increase the number of polynomial terms in each element so that the shape functions can span a larger space of polynomial functions. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `BlocksDimensions` | Sets the number of blocks of cells in each direction. A cell block may be divided into multiple cells (e.g. there will be 6 pyramid cells in a cell block). If a 1D cell type is chosen only the first blocks dimension will be used. If a 2D cell type is chosen the first and second blocks dimensions will be used. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `CellOrder` | This property specifies the interpolation order for Lagrange cell types. | `{"maximum":10,"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `CellType` | This property specifies the type of cells to generate. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Line","Quadratic Line","Cubic Line","Triangle","Quad","Pixel","Polygon","Quadratic Triangle","Quadratic Quad","Bi-Quadratic Quad","Tet","Hex","Polyhedron","Voxel","Wedge","Pyramid","Quadratic Tet","Quadratic Hex","Tri-Quadratic Hexahedron","Quadratic Wedge","Quadratic Pyramid","Tri-Quadratic Pyramid","Lagrange Curve","Lagrange Triangle","Lagrange Quadrilateral","Lagrange Tetrahedron","Lagrange Hexahedron","Lagrange Wedge","Bezier Curve","Bezier Triangle","Bezier Quadrilateral","Bezier Tetrahedron","Bezier Hexahedron","Bezier Wedge"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Line"` |
| `OutputPrecision` | This property specifies the precision of point locations and fields. | `{"type":"enum","values":["Single","Double"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"Single"` |
| `PolynomialFieldOrder` | This property specifies the order for the "Polynomial" point data field. | `{"minimum":0,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0` |
